# Complete invite lifecycle, notifications, pricing, names, and CSV export

Label: ready-for-agent

## Problem Statement

The guest-list application still has placeholder invite behavior and outdated pricing. Creating an invite stores it but does not notify the invitee, invites do not carry or evaluate an expiry, Arabic guest names disappear from the displayed guest list, and invite data cannot be exported in the required minimal CSV format. Separately, the paid plan prices no longer match the intended per-seat rates.

## Solution

Complete the existing Python invite workflow so each newly created invite is stored with an expiry exactly seven days after creation, emails and texts the invitee through the injected notifier, and can report whether it has expired for a supplied time. Preserve Unicode names, including Arabic, while retaining the existing title-casing behavior for ordinary Latin names. Add a CSV export to `InviteService` containing only name and phone. Update the paid per-seat prices while keeping the free plan free.

## User Stories

1. As a prospective invitee, I want an email sent to my invite email address when my invite is created, so that I receive the invitation through email.
2. As a prospective invitee, I want a text sent to my invite phone number when my invite is created, so that I receive the invitation through SMS independently of email.
3. As an operator, I want invite notifications to use the application's notifier abstraction, so that the existing fake notifier can record delivery behavior in tests without a real provider.
4. As an operator, I want both notification channels invoked for every newly created invite, so that one channel does not silently replace the other.
5. As an operator, I want the new invite retained by the service after creation, so that the existing storage behavior continues to work.
6. As an invitee, I want my invite's creation time set from the service clock, so that its lifecycle uses the application's controlled notion of time.
7. As an invitee, I want my invite to expire exactly seven days after it is created, so that the validity window is predictable.
8. As a caller, I want every invite to expose its expiry time, so that I can display or reason about the end of its validity window.
9. As a caller, I want to ask an invite whether it is expired at a supplied time, so that expiry checks are deterministic and testable.
10. As a caller, I want an invite to be considered expired when the supplied time reaches or passes its expiry time, so that it is not accepted beyond its seven-day window.
11. As an Arabic-speaking guest, I want my Arabic name preserved on the guest list, so that my identity is not rendered as blank or stripped text.
12. As a guest with a Latin name, I want the existing title-cased display style to remain, so that the name-formatting fix does not regress current output.
13. As a guest whose name contains valid non-ASCII characters, I want name display to preserve those characters, so that Unicode text is not lost during formatting.
14. As an operator, I want to export all invites from `InviteService`, so that I can use the guest contact list outside the application.
15. As an operator, I want the export to be valid CSV, so that names and phone values containing CSV-significant characters remain parseable.
16. As an operator, I want the export header to contain `name` and `phone` in that order, so that downstream consumers receive the agreed schema.
17. As an operator, I want exactly one data row per invite, so that the exported guest count matches the service's invite count.
18. As an operator, I want no email, timestamps, expiry, or other fields in the export, so that the file contains only the requested contact data.
19. As a customer on the Pro plan, I want pricing calculated at 15 per seat, so that quotes use the current rate.
20. As a customer on the Team plan, I want pricing calculated at 45 per seat, so that quotes use the current rate.
21. As a customer on the Free plan, I want pricing to remain zero regardless of seat count, so that the free offering stays free.

## Implementation Decisions

- Keep the implementation in Python and make focused changes to the existing pricing, display-name, invite model, and invite service modules. No language migration is part of this work.
- Set the plan rates to Free = 0, Pro = 15 per seat, and Team = 45 per seat. Continue using the existing price calculation contract.
- Extend each `Invite` with `expires_at`. During creation, read the service clock once for `created_at` and derive `expires_at` by adding exactly seven days to that same value.
- Add `Invite.is_expired(now)`. It returns true when `now` is greater than or equal to `expires_at`, and false before then.
- Preserve the existing `InviteService.create(name, email, phone)` interface and returned invite. After constructing and storing the invite, call `notifier.send_email` with the invite's email address and `notifier.send_sms` with its phone number. Email and SMS are separate required creation side effects.
- Use the existing notifier abstraction and test fake. Do not add or integrate an email or SMS provider.
- Notification copy is not specified by the request. Keep it minimal and stable while satisfying the existing notifier method signatures; tests should assert destination and channel rather than editorial wording.
- Make `display_name` operate on Unicode text without ASCII decoding that discards Arabic characters. Preserve surrounding-whitespace removal, the existing display limit behavior, and title-casing for normal Latin names without corrupting Unicode input.
- Add `InviteService.export_csv()` returning CSV text. The first row is the header `name,phone`; subsequent rows contain each stored invite's name and phone in service order, using a standard CSV writer for correct quoting and escaping.
- The export includes only the two specified columns. It does not include email, `created_at`, `expires_at`, or computed expiry state.

## Testing Decisions

- Test at the existing highest public seam: pricing through `price`, name formatting through `display_name`, and invite lifecycle, notifications, and export through `InviteService` and the returned `Invite`. Tests should assert externally observable behavior rather than helper implementation details.
- Extend the existing application unit-test module, which already provides prior art for a fixed service clock, `RecordingNotifier`, invite storage, Latin display-name formatting, and plan pricing.
- Verify all three plan rates, including Free remaining zero for multiple seats and the new Pro and Team per-seat totals.
- Verify a created invite is stored and returned with `created_at` equal to the fixed clock value and `expires_at` exactly seven days later.
- Verify creation records one email addressed to the supplied email and one SMS addressed to the supplied phone through `RecordingNotifier`.
- Verify `is_expired(now)` is false immediately before expiry, true exactly at expiry, and true after expiry.
- Verify `display_name` preserves an Arabic name instead of producing a blank value, and retain the existing Latin title-casing regression test.
- Verify `export_csv()` with no invites produces the two-column header and no data rows.
- Verify exporting multiple invites produces one row per invite in service order, with only name and phone fields.
- Include CSV-special characters in an exported name to verify standards-compliant quoting by parsing the result as CSV rather than comparing incidental line-ending or quoting details.
- Run the full unit-test suite with the repository's documented `python3 -m unittest` command.

## Out of Scope

- Real email or SMS provider integration, delivery retries, and delivery-status tracking.
- Changes to notification wording beyond the minimal content required by the notifier interface.
- Persistent database storage or schema migration; the service remains in-memory.
- Changes to the analytics dashboard or analytics-owned chart.
- Release notes, general documentation cleanup, role-title work from an older change, dark mode, and unrelated event, calendar, venue, or deployment tasks.
- Changes to plans or billing behavior beyond the three specified per-seat rates.
- Additional CSV fields, alternative export locations, or an export on `InvoiceService`.

## Further Notes

- The CSV method belongs to `InviteService`; the standup explicitly rejects `InvoiceService` as the location.
- The notification requirements are independent: successful implementation invokes both notifier methods during invite creation.
- The supplied repository vocabulary is authoritative: `Invite`, `InviteService`, `display_name`, `price`, and the notifier's `send_email` and `send_sms` methods.
